description: An application that provides notifications regarding environmental problems or disasters, using data from NASA—a tool that government ministries could utilize
summary:
We developed Bahrain EcoScope, a web app that turns NASA satellite data into clear answers about our homeland: what is changing, where, and whether the change is real. Users explore Bahrain's four governorates, and warning icons appear on the map wherever there is an environmental problem, showing us the problem along with suggested solutions and the authority responsible for acting.

The app addresses the challenge by turning complex NASA data into understandable scientific evidence, tested statistically to confirm it is reliable. Our analysis shows that nighttime temperatures are rising fastest in all four governorates. We use AI to suggest solutions and show how places could look after they are applied, while the facts always come from NASA.

Our project matters because it helps government authorities make informed decisions, and it raises people's awareness of the environmental problems around them and encourages them to take part in making a difference. It runs on any device with nothing to install, and it can be expanded to serve any country. We started with Bahrain, because home comes  first.
details:
What does it do and how does it work?

Bahrain EcoScope is a web app that turns NASA satellite data into clear answers about Bahrain: what is changing, where, and whether the change is real. Users explore the four governorates and discover their environmental problems. A warning (danger) icon appears on the map whenever there is a problem in an area, and when we tap it, the problem appears along with solutions, suggestions, and the responsible authorities. The Trend Detective tool tests changes statistically (Mann-Kendall test, with Sen's slope for the rate of change) using NASA MODIS data from 2001 to 2025. The app then connects each finding to the problem, the suggested solution, and the authority that can act. It also sends alerts about affected areas. Our analysis shows that nighttime temperatures are rising fastest in all four governorates, by about 0.8 to 1.3 °C per decade.

What benefits does it have?

For ministries and authorities: clear evidence, monitoring of environmental problems, identification of the most affected areas, and tracking of change over time, which supports informed decisions

For the people: a better understanding of the environmental problems around them, greater awareness, and encouragement to take part in making a difference

What is the intended impact?

To help build a cleaner, greener, and more sustainable Bahrain for future generations, by giving authorities and citizens a shared, science-based view of the environment. We also plan to expand EcoScope worldwide, so any country can load its own borders and discover what is changing in its land.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

Programming languages: We used many languages, most notably HTML, CSS, and JavaScript

Coding environment: We used Visual Studio Code (VS Code) to write the code

NASA data: NASA MODIS Terra data (MOD11A2.061 for land surface temperature, MOD13Q1.061 for the EVI vegetation index), accessed through NASA AppEEARS

Statistical analysis: Mann-Kendall test

Artificial intelligence: To suggest solutions and generate images showing how places could look after those solutions are applied

How it runs: A web-browser-based app that works on a computer, tablet, or phone with nothing to install

How is your project creative?

It combines space technology with local environmental needs, which sets it apart from other environmental apps

It shows interactive warning icons on the map that reveal environmental problems instantly and link them to solutions and suggestions

It uses AI to show how a place could look after solutions such as more trees and green spaces, so people can picture a greener Bahrain

Its "Data to Action" approach links every finding to a problem, a solution, and the responsible authority

Its guiding principle: "AI helps us, but the facts come from NASA"

What factors did your team consider?

Scientific accuracy: Facts come from real NASA data, and trends are tested for statistical significance (95% confidence) rather than just displayed

Accessibility: It works in any browser on any device, with no installation

Users: Ministries, researchers, schools and students, and ordinary citizens

Actionability: Each problem is paired with a practical solution and the right authority

Scalability: It is designed so that it can grow beyond Bahrain

Responsible AI use: AI supports the science and does not replace it
